title: Organising a small app

notes: State is one variable; logic never touches the page.
dispense returns a new array or throws a clear error.
The listener is the glue, and the status line is aria-live so changes are announced.

exercises.title: Pure stock logic
exercises.prompt: Write two pure functions for clinic stock (an array like [{ name: "ORS", qty: 30 }]). Neither may change the array or objects it is given. receive(stock, name, qty): if qty isn't a number above 0, throw new Error("Quantity must be more than 0"); if an item with that name exists (ignore case and spaces around the name), return a new array where its qty is increased; otherwise return a new array with { name: (trimmed), qty } added at the end. dispense(stock, name, qty): same quantity check; if the item doesn't exist or has less than qty, throw new Error("Not enough NAME") (the name as given, trimmed); otherwise return a new array with its qty reduced.

tests.call: (() => { try { dispense([{ name: "ORS", qty: 30 }, { name: "Gloves", qty: 100 }], "ORS", 31); return "no error"; } catch (e) { return e.message; } })()
tests.name: not enough

tests.call: [() => dispense([{ name: "ORS", qty: 30 }, { name: "Gloves", qty: 100 }], "Zinc", 1), () => receive([], "ORS", 0), () => dispense([{ name: "ORS", qty: 30 }, { name: "Gloves", qty: 100 }], "ORS", -2)].map((f) => { try { f(); return "no error"; } catch (e) { return e.message; } })
tests.name: unknown items and bad quantities
the original is never changed
tests.hint_if_fail: Use map with { ...item, qty: ... } and [...stock, newItem].

hints: A helper: const same = (item) => item.name.toLowerCase() === name.trim().toLowerCase();
Quantity check first: if (!Number.isFinite(qty) || qty <= 0) throw new Error("Quantity must be more than 0");
return stock.map((i) => (same(i) ? { ...i, qty: i.qty + qty } : i)); and for a new one return [...stock, { name: name.trim(), qty }];

exercises.title: A tiny module
exercises.prompt: Build a savings group (chama) as a module: var Chama = (function () { ... })(); keeping the members and their totals PRIVATE inside (a Map works well), and returning an object with five functions. join(name): trims the name; returns false for a blank name or one already joined, otherwise adds the member with 0 paid and returns true. pay(name, amount): throws new Error("NAME is not a member") for an unknown name, throws new Error("Amount must be more than 0") if amount isn't a number above 0, otherwise adds it and returns that member's new total. balanceOf(name): that member's total (0 for an unknown name). total(): everything paid by everyone. names(): the member names sorted A to Z.

tests.hint_if_fail: join trims the name, so " Juma " joins as "Juma".

tests.name: no doubles, blanks, and private state
tests.hint_if_fail: Keep the Map inside the function; don't return it.

tests.call: [() => Chama.pay("Zawadi", 100), () => Chama.pay("Juma", 0), () => Chama.pay("Juma", "abc")].map((f) => { try { f(); return "no error"; } catch (e) { return e.message; } }).concat([Chama.total()])

hints: const members = new Map(); inside the function, before join.
join: const clean = name.trim(); if (clean === "" || members.has(clean)) return false; members.set(clean, 0); return true;
total: [...members.values()].reduce((s, v) => s + v, 0); names: [...members.keys()].sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b))

exercises.title: A page everyone can use
exercises.prompt: This clinic queue page works with a mouse, but not with a keyboard or a screen reader. Fix it: wrap the content in <main>; put the input inside <form id="add-form"> with a <label for="patient">; replace the clickable div with a real <button type="submit">; give #status aria-live="polite" so changes are announced; and remove every inline onclick (ex3_queue.js already wires the form's submit event). Keep the ids patient, queue and status, and the script tag.

quiz.why: Its answer depends only on its argument and it changes nothing outside.

quiz.q: Where should the rule "you can't dispense more than you have" live?
choices: In a logic function like dispense()
quiz.why: Rules go in logic; render only draws.

quiz.q: In const C = (function () { let n = 0; return { add() { n++; } }; })(); what is C.n?
quiz.why: n is private to the function; only add can reach it (a closure).

quiz.q: Your code updates a status message, but screen reader users never hear it. The fix?
choices: Put it in an element with aria-live="polite" (or role="status")
quiz.why: Live regions are announced when their content changes.

quiz.q: Why a <button> rather than a <div onclick>?
choices: Buttons work with the keyboard and announce themselves to screen readers
quiz.why: Real controls come with keyboard and accessibility support for free.
